KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T1_MAAMKUZI_NA_MAAGANO.MA.error: Answers a greeting with the same greeting (Hujambo? Hujambo!) instead of its reply.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T1_MAAMKUZI_NA_MAAGANO.MA.cause: The child hears the greeting as a sound to echo, as with "Hello" in English; the question-and-answer pair has not been learnt.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T1_MAAMKUZI_NA_MAAGANO.MA.reveals: The question "Rafiki anakusalimu: "Hujambo?" Unajibu nini?" with "Hujambo" among the options.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T1_MAAMKUZI_NA_MAAGANO.MA.help: Act it as a ball game: the greeting is thrown, the reply is caught; the two words are on two different cards.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T1_MAAMKUZI_NA_MAAGANO.MA.feedback: Ukiulizwa "Hujambo?" unajibu "Sijambo," maana yake sina tatizo.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T1_MAAMKUZI_NA_MAAGANO.MA.source: English or mother-tongue interference on Kiswahili; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T1_MAAMKUZI_NA_MAAGANO.MA.error: Greets an elder with a peer or Sheng greeting (Mambo! Sasa!) instead of Shikamoo.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T1_MAAMKUZI_NA_MAAGANO.MA.cause: Mambo and Sasa are what the child hears most among children and on the street; he has not been taught that an elder is greeted differently.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T1_MAAMKUZI_NA_MAAGANO.MA.reveals: The question "Unamwona babu njiani. Unamsalimu vipi?" with "Mambo babu!" among the options.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T1_MAAMKUZI_NA_MAAGANO.MA.help: Sort picture cards of people (babu, rafiki, mwalimu) into two piles: Shikamoo and Hujambo.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T1_MAAMKUZI_NA_MAAGANO.MA.feedback: Mzee husalimiwa kwa heshima: Shikamoo babu!
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T1_MAAMKUZI_NA_MAAGANO.MA.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T1_MAAMKUZI_NA_MAAGANO.MA.error: Gives the elder's reply to the child's greeting the wrong way round (the elder says Shikamoo, or the child says Marahaba).

example.question: Mtoto anamsalimu bibi: "Shikamoo bibi!" Bibi anajibu nini?

KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T1_MAAMKUZI_NA_MAAGANO.MA.cause: Both words are heard together and the child does not yet know which belongs to the young person and which to the elder.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T1_MAAMKUZI_NA_MAAGANO.MA.reveals: The question "Mtoto anamsalimu bibi: "Shikamoo bibi!" Bibi anajibu nini?" with "Shikamoo" among the options.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T1_MAAMKUZI_NA_MAAGANO.MA.help: Role-play with a hat for the elder: only the one with the hat may say Marahaba.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T1_MAAMKUZI_NA_MAAGANO.MA.feedback: Mtoto anasema Shikamoo; mzee anajibu Marahaba.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T1_MAAMKUZI_NA_MAAGANO.MA.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T1_MAAMKUZI_NA_MAAGANO.MA.error: Uses the greeting of another time of day.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T1_MAAMKUZI_NA_MAAGANO.MA.cause: The child learnt one greeting as a set phrase and uses it at every hour.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T1_MAAMKUZI_NA_MAAGANO.MA.reveals: The question "Unamwona mwalimu asubuhi. Unamsalimu vipi?" with "Habari za jioni mwalimu!" among the options.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T1_MAAMKUZI_NA_MAAGANO.MA.help: A clock or sun chart: asubuhi, mchana, jioni, usiku; the child moves the arrow and says the greeting for that time.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T1_MAAMKUZI_NA_MAAGANO.MA.feedback: Salamu hufuata wakati: Habari za asubuhi mwalimu!
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T1_MAAMKUZI_NA_MAAGANO.MA.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T1_MAAMKUZI_NA_MAAGANO.MA.error: Uses a greeting when leaving, or a farewell when arriving.

example.question: Unaenda nyumbani baada ya shule. Unamuaga mwalimu vipi?

KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T1_MAAMKUZI_NA_MAAGANO.MA.cause: Greeting and farewell words are learnt on one chart and the child mixes the two columns.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T1_MAAMKUZI_NA_MAAGANO.MA.reveals: The question "Unaenda nyumbani baada ya shule. Unamuaga mwalimu vipi?" with "Hujambo mwalimu!" among the options.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T1_MAAMKUZI_NA_MAAGANO.MA.help: Act out a door: walk in and greet, walk out and say goodbye.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T1_MAAMKUZI_NA_MAAGANO.MA.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T1_MAAMKUZI_NA_MAAGANO.MA.error: Greets a group with the singular greeting (Hujambo?) or answers for a group with Sijambo.

example.question: Mwalimu anaingia darasani na kusema: "Hamjambo wanafunzi?" Darasa linajibu nini?

KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T1_MAAMKUZI_NA_MAAGANO.MA.cause: The child knows one pair only; the plural forms hamjambo/hatujambo follow the person marker (m-, tu-), which has not been noticed.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T1_MAAMKUZI_NA_MAAGANO.MA.reveals: The question "Mwalimu anaingia darasani na kusema: "Hamjambo wanafunzi?" Darasa linajibu nini?" with "Sijambo" among the options.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T1_MAAMKUZI_NA_MAAGANO.MA.help: Greet one child, then the whole row; show that the word changes with one or many.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T1_MAAMKUZI_NA_MAAGANO.MA.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T1_USOMAJI_MWAFAKA.USOMAJ.error: Starts reading from the right or from the bottom of the page.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T1_USOMAJI_MWAFAKA.USOMAJ.cause: Some children have seen other scripts read from the right, or simply start where the picture is.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T1_USOMAJI_MWAFAKA.USOMAJ.reveals: The question "Unaanza kusoma ukurasa kutoka wapi?" with "chini upande wa kulia" among the options.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T1_USOMAJI_MWAFAKA.USOMAJ.help: Put a green dot at the top left of each page: start at the green dot.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T1_USOMAJI_MWAFAKA.USOMAJ.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T1_USOMAJI_MWAFAKA.USOMAJ.error: Holds the book upside down or back to front.

example.question: Kitabu kiko sawa lini?
example.correct_answer: picha na maandishi yakiwa wima, jalada mbele

KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T1_USOMAJI_MWAFAKA.USOMAJ.cause: The child has handled few books and does not check the picture before reading.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T1_USOMAJI_MWAFAKA.USOMAJ.reveals: The question "Kitabu kiko sawa lini?" with "picha zikiwa juu chini" among the options.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T1_USOMAJI_MWAFAKA.USOMAJ.help: Before opening, find the front cover and check that the people in the picture stand up.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T1_USOMAJI_MWAFAKA.USOMAJ.feedback: Shika kitabu wima: jalada mbele, picha zimesimama.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T1_USOMAJI_MWAFAKA.USOMAJ.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T1_USOMAJI_MWAFAKA.USOMAJ.error: Reads lying on the desk with his face almost on the page, or leaning back far from it.

example.question: Mkao upi ni bora unaposoma?
example.wrong_answer: kulala juu ya meza uso karibu na kitabu
example.correct_answer: kuketi wima, kitabu mezani umbali wa mkono

KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T1_USOMAJI_MWAFAKA.USOMAJ.cause: The child is tired or cannot see well; nobody has shown the reading position.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T1_USOMAJI_MWAFAKA.USOMAJ.reveals: The question "Mkao upi ni bora unaposoma?" with "kulala juu ya meza uso karibu na kitabu" among the options.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T1_USOMAJI_MWAFAKA.USOMAJ.help: Show the "elbow distance": the book is as far as from the elbow to the hand. If the child still leans in, tell the parent to check the eyes.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T1_USOMAJI_MWAFAKA.USOMAJ.feedback: Keti wima, kitabu kiwe umbali wa kiwiko hadi kiganja.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T1_USOMAJI_MWAFAKA.USOMAJ.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T1_USOMAJI_MWAFAKA.USOMAJ.error: Loses the line and jumps to another line or back to the start.

example.question: Unapomaliza mstari wa kwanza, unaenda wapi?
example.correct_answer: mwanzo wa mstari wa pili, upande wa kushoto

KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T1_USOMAJI_MWAFAKA.USOMAJ.cause: The eye sweep back to the next line is new; without a finger guide the child lands anywhere.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T1_USOMAJI_MWAFAKA.USOMAJ.reveals: The question "Unapomaliza mstari wa kwanza, unaenda wapi?" with "popote ninapoona neno ninalolijua" among the options.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T1_USOMAJI_MWAFAKA.USOMAJ.help: Move a finger or a card under the line; at the end, slide back to the left and down one line.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T1_USOMAJI_MWAFAKA.USOMAJ.feedback: Mwisho wa mstari, rudi kushoto kwenye mstari unaofuata.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T1_USOMAJI_MWAFAKA.USOMAJ.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUANDI.T1_UANDISHI_BORA.UANDISHI.error: Grips the pencil in the fist, or with all the fingers wrapped round it.

example.question: Kalamu inashikwa vipi?
example.correct_answer: kwa kidole gumba na vidole viwili

KISW.G1.KUANDI.T1_UANDISHI_BORA.UANDISHI.cause: A fist grip is how small children first hold a crayon; the tripod grip has not been taught.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T1_UANDISHI_BORA.UANDISHI.reveals: The question "Kalamu inashikwa vipi?" with "kwa ngumi nzima" among the options.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T1_UANDISHI_BORA.UANDISHI.help: Pinch the pencil with thumb and pointer, rest it on the middle finger; a small rubber band can mark the place.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T1_UANDISHI_BORA.UANDISHI.feedback: Shika kalamu kwa vidole vitatu, si kwa ngumi.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T1_UANDISHI_BORA.UANDISHI.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUANDI.T1_UANDISHI_BORA.UANDISHI.error: Writes with the head on the desk or the body twisted, the book at an angle.

example.question: Mkao upi ni bora unapoandika?
example.correct_answer: kuketi wima, miguu sakafuni, daftari limenyooka

KISW.G1.KUANDI.T1_UANDISHI_BORA.UANDISHI.cause: The child tires quickly and nobody has shown the writing position.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T1_UANDISHI_BORA.UANDISHI.reveals: The question "Mkao upi ni bora unapoandika?" with "kichwa juu ya meza" among the options.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T1_UANDISHI_BORA.UANDISHI.help: Check four things before writing: back straight, feet down, book straight, free hand holding the page.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T1_UANDISHI_BORA.UANDISHI.feedback: Keti wima na unyooshe daftari kabla ya kuandika.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T1_UANDISHI_BORA.UANDISHI.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUANDI.T1_UANDISHI_BORA.UANDISHI.error: Starts writing at the right of the line, or writes letters from right to left.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T1_UANDISHI_BORA.UANDISHI.cause: The child starts wherever there is space, or copies the direction of a sibling's writing in another script.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T1_UANDISHI_BORA.UANDISHI.reveals: The question "Unaanza kuandika mstari kutoka wapi?" with "upande wa kulia" among the options.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T1_UANDISHI_BORA.UANDISHI.help: A green start line at the left margin of each line.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T1_UANDISHI_BORA.UANDISHI.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUANDI.T1_UANDISHI_BORA.UANDISHI.error: Presses so hard the pencil breaks or tears the page.

example.question: Unaandika kwa nguvu kiasi gani?
example.wrong_answer: kwa nguvu sana mpaka karatasi ikatike

KISW.G1.KUANDI.T1_UANDISHI_BORA.UANDISHI.cause: The child holds the pencil too tight from worry or from the fist grip.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T1_UANDISHI_BORA.UANDISHI.reveals: The question "Unaandika kwa nguvu kiasi gani?" with "kwa nguvu sana mpaka karatasi ikatike" among the options.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T1_UANDISHI_BORA.UANDISHI.help: Write on a sheet with carbon or soft paper below; the mark should not come through.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T1_UANDISHI_BORA.UANDISHI.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.SARUFI.T1_MATUMIZI_YA_MIMI_NA_.N.error: The pronoun and the subject marker on the verb do not agree (Wao anacheza).
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T1_MATUMIZI_YA_MIMI_NA_.N.cause: The child learns the pronoun as a word and the verb as a fixed form; he has not seen that the verb changes with the person.
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T1_MATUMIZI_YA_MIMI_NA_.N.reveals: The question "Jaza: Sisi ___ (imba) wimbo." with "ninaimba" among the options.
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T1_MATUMIZI_YA_MIMI_NA_.N.help: Colour the pronoun and the verb's first syllable the same colour: yeye a-, wao wa-, mimi ni-, sisi tu-, wewe u-, nyinyi m-.
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T1_MATUMIZI_YA_MIMI_NA_.N.feedback: Kitendo hufuata nafsi: Wao wanacheza; Yeye anacheza. (tunaimba)
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T1_MATUMIZI_YA_MIMI_NA_.N.source: English or mother-tongue interference on Kiswahili; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.SARUFI.T1_MATUMIZI_YA_MIMI_NA_.N.error: Uses the one-person pronoun for many people, or the reverse.
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T1_MATUMIZI_YA_MIMI_NA_.N.cause: The child has not linked the pronoun pair to one and many.
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T1_MATUMIZI_YA_MIMI_NA_.N.reveals: The question "Mimi na Ali tunacheza. ___ tunacheza." with "Mimi" among the options.
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T1_MATUMIZI_YA_MIMI_NA_.N.help: Point at one child, then at a group, saying the right pronoun each time.
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T1_MATUMIZI_YA_MIMI_NA_.N.feedback: Mtu mmoja ni yeye; watu wengi ni wao. (Sisi)
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T1_MATUMIZI_YA_MIMI_NA_.N.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.SARUFI.T1_MATUMIZI_YA_MIMI_NA_.N.error: Repeats the pronoun of the question in the answer (Wewe unaenda wapi? Wewe ninaenda sokoni.) instead of switching to mimi.
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T1_MATUMIZI_YA_MIMI_NA_.N.cause: The child copies the words he heard; changing person between speakers is new.
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T1_MATUMIZI_YA_MIMI_NA_.N.reveals: The question "Mwalimu anakuuliza: "Unaitwa nani?" Unajibu:" with "Wewe ni Baraka." among the options.
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T1_MATUMIZI_YA_MIMI_NA_.N.help: Ask and answer in pairs with a pointing finger: wewe points out, mimi points to the chest.
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T1_MATUMIZI_YA_MIMI_NA_.N.feedback: Ukiulizwa kwa "wewe", unajibu kwa "mimi". (Mimi ni Baraka.)
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T1_MATUMIZI_YA_MIMI_NA_.N.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.SARUFI.T1_MATUMIZI_YA_MIMI_NA_.N.error: Puts the pronoun after the verb instead of the object marker inside it (Mama alimpa mimi for Mama alinipa).
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T1_MATUMIZI_YA_MIMI_NA_.N.cause: English says "gave me"; the child adds the separate word instead of -ni- inside the verb.
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T1_MATUMIZI_YA_MIMI_NA_.N.reveals: The question "Ni lipi sahihi?" with "Mama alimpa mimi chakula." among the options.
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T1_MATUMIZI_YA_MIMI_NA_.N.help: Show the verb with the object marker coloured: a-li-ni-pa; compare with the wrong form.
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T1_MATUMIZI_YA_MIMI_NA_.N.feedback: Tunasema "Mama alinipa", si "alimpa mimi". (Mama alinipa chakula.)
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T1_MATUMIZI_YA_MIMI_NA_.N.source: English or mother-tongue interference on Kiswahili; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

example.question: Mwalimu anasema "lala". Neno lipi limetamkwa vizuri?

KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T2_MATAMSHI_BORA.MATAMSHI.cause: Many Kenyan first languages have no /l/, or do not separate it from /r/; the child puts in the home sound.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T2_MATAMSHI_BORA.MATAMSHI.reveals: The question "Mwalimu anasema "lala". Neno lipi limetamkwa vizuri?" with "rara" among the options.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T2_MATAMSHI_BORA.MATAMSHI.help: Say the two side by side, slowly, watching the mouth; the child holds up a card for the sound he hears.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T2_MATAMSHI_BORA.MATAMSHI.source: mother-tongue sound interference common in Kenyan classrooms; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T2_MATAMSHI_BORA.MATAMSHI.cause: /k/ and /g/ are close; a first language with only one of them puts that one in both places.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T2_MATAMSHI_BORA.MATAMSHI.reveals: The question "Neno lipi limetamkwa vizuri?" with "gaga" among the options.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T2_MATAMSHI_BORA.MATAMSHI.help: Contrast the two with a mirror and a hand before the mouth; the child says which he hears.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T2_MATAMSHI_BORA.MATAMSHI.source: mother-tongue sound interference common in Kenyan classrooms; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T2_MATAMSHI_BORA.MATAMSHI.error: Splits "mama" by letters rather than by syllables (each Kiswahili syllable ends in a vowel).
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T2_MATAMSHI_BORA.MATAMSHI.cause: The child has learnt letters one by one and has not been shown that a syllable is a sound that ends in a vowel.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T2_MATAMSHI_BORA.MATAMSHI.reveals: The question "Neno "mama" lina silabi zipi?" with "m-a-m-a" among the options.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T2_MATAMSHI_BORA.MATAMSHI.help: Clap the word: one clap per vowel; the consonants go with the vowel after them.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T2_MATAMSHI_BORA.MATAMSHI.feedback: Kila silabi ya Kiswahili huishia kwa irabu: ma-ma.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T2_MATAMSHI_BORA.MATAMSHI.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T2_MATAMSHI_BORA.MATAMSHI.error: Says the English letter name instead of the Kiswahili sound (/m/ as "em"), so the syllable cannot be built.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T2_MATAMSHI_BORA.MATAMSHI.cause: English letter names are taught alongside and the child brings them to Kiswahili; a syllable is built from sounds, not names.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T2_MATAMSHI_BORA.MATAMSHI.reveals: The question "Sauti ya herufi "m" ni ipi?" with "em" among the options.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T2_MATAMSHI_BORA.MATAMSHI.help: Say the sound alone, short (/m/), then join it to a vowel: ma, me, mi.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T2_MATAMSHI_BORA.MATAMSHI.source: English or mother-tongue interference on Kiswahili; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T2_MATAMSHI_BORA.MATAMSHI.error: Picks a word with no target sound when asked for one that has it.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T2_MATAMSHI_BORA.MATAMSHI.cause: The child looks at the first letter or the picture, not at the sound.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T2_MATAMSHI_BORA.MATAMSHI.reveals: The question "Ni neno lipi lina sauti /m/, /a/, /u/, /k/, /t/, /l/?" with "baba" among the options.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T2_MATAMSHI_BORA.MATAMSHI.help: Underline the target sound in each word on the card before choosing.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T2_MATAMSHI_BORA.MATAMSHI.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T2_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA.KUS.error: Reads the target word wrongly: "kuku" as "guku".
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T2_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA.KUS.cause: The child reads the letters with the sounds of his first language, or adds a vowel to break the cluster.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T2_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA.KUS.reveals: The question "Neno "kuku" linasomwa vipi?" with "guku" among the options.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T2_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA.KUS.help: Pick out the target words before reading; practise them on cards, then read the passage.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T2_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA.KUS.source: mother-tongue sound interference common in Kenyan classrooms; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T2_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA.KUS.error: Reads word by word or syllable by syllable, so the sentence has no meaning when heard.

example.question: Ni usomaji upi ni wa ufasaha: "Mama ana kuku."?

KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T2_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA.KUS.cause: The child is still decoding each word; he has not yet read a group of words as one piece.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T2_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA.KUS.reveals: The question "Ni usomaji upi ni wa ufasaha: "Mama ana kuku."?" with "Mama ... ana ... kuku." among the options.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T2_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA.KUS.help: Echo reading: the teacher reads a phrase, the child repeats it in one breath.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T2_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA.KUS.feedback: Soma maneno kwa pamoja kama unavyozungumza.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T2_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA.KUS.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T2_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA.KUS.error: Reads so softly (or so loudly, shouting) that the class cannot follow.

example.question: Unaposoma mbele ya darasa, sauti yako inafaa kuwa vipi?
example.wrong_answer: ya chini ili nisikosee mbele ya wenzangu
example.correct_answer: ya kusikika na wote darasani, bila kupiga kelele

KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T2_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA.KUS.cause: Shyness, or the belief that reading well means reading loud.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T2_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA.KUS.reveals: The question "Unaposoma mbele ya darasa, sauti yako inafaa kuwa vipi?" with "ya chini ili nisikosee mbele ya wenzangu" among the options.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T2_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA.KUS.help: Stand the reader at the front and a listener at the back: the listener raises a hand when he hears every word.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T2_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA.KUS.feedback: Soma kwa sauti inayosikika na wote, bila kupiga kelele.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T2_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA.KUS.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T2_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA.KUS.error: Reads as fast as possible and thinks the fastest reader is the best.

example.question: Kasi ifaayo ya kusoma kifungu ni ipi?
example.correct_answer: kasi ya kuzungumza, karibu maneno 5 kwa dakika

KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T2_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA.KUS.cause: Reading races in class reward speed; nobody asked whether the listeners understood.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T2_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA.KUS.reveals: The question "Kasi ifaayo ya kusoma kifungu ni ipi?" with "haraka iwezekanavyo" among the options.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T2_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA.KUS.help: Time two readings, one very fast and one at speaking pace; the listeners answer one question after each.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T2_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA.KUS.feedback: Kasi ifaayo ni ya kuzungumza: si haraka mno, si polepole mno.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T2_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA.KUS.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T2_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA.KUS.error: Reads a question in the flat voice of a statement and runs on through the koma and kikomo.

example.question: Sentensi "Je, kaka yuko?" inasomwa vipi?
example.wrong_answer: kwa sauti ileile ya sentensi ya kawaida
example.correct_answer: sauti hupanda mwishoni kwa sababu ni swali

KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T2_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA.KUS.cause: The child looks at the words and not at the marks.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T2_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA.KUS.reveals: The question "Sentensi "Je, kaka yuko?" inasomwa vipi?" with "kwa sauti ileile ya sentensi ya kawaida" among the options.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T2_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA.KUS.help: Read the same words three ways (. ? !); the child points at the mark that fits each reading; clap at each kikomo.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T2_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA.KUS.feedback: Kiulizi (?) hupandisha sauti mwishoni; simama kidogo kwenye koma na kikomo.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T2_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA.KUS.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUANDI.T2_HATI_NADHIFU_HERUFI_.H.error: Starts a sentence or a name with a small letter.

example.question: Andika kwa usahihi: mama na baba wako nyumbani.

KISW.G1.KUANDI.T2_HATI_NADHIFU_HERUFI_.H.cause: The child copies words, not sentences; the rule that a sentence and a name begin with a capital is not yet used.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T2_HATI_NADHIFU_HERUFI_.H.reveals: The question "Andika kwa usahihi: mama na baba wako nyumbani." with "mama na baba wako nyumbani." among the options.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T2_HATI_NADHIFU_HERUFI_.H.help: Circle the first letter of each sentence and each name in a passage in red.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T2_HATI_NADHIFU_HERUFI_.H.feedback: Sentensi na jina la mtu au mahali huanza kwa herufi kubwa.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T2_HATI_NADHIFU_HERUFI_.H.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUANDI.T2_HATI_NADHIFU_HERUFI_.H.error: Puts capital letters in the middle of words (JuMa, Kitabu KiKubwa).
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T2_HATI_NADHIFU_HERUFI_.H.cause: Some capitals (K, M, S) are easier to form than the small letter, so the child uses them anywhere.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T2_HATI_NADHIFU_HERUFI_.H.reveals: The question "Ni lipi limeandikwa vizuri?" with "JuMa ANakula" among the options.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T2_HATI_NADHIFU_HERUFI_.H.help: Sort letter cards: capital only at the start; the rest small.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T2_HATI_NADHIFU_HERUFI_.H.feedback: Herufi kubwa iko mwanzoni tu; nyingine ni ndogo.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T2_HATI_NADHIFU_HERUFI_.H.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUANDI.T2_HATI_NADHIFU_HERUFI_.H.cause: Spoken Kiswahili runs words together; the child writes the stream as he hears it.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T2_HATI_NADHIFU_HERUFI_.H.reveals: The question "Ni lipi limeandikwa vizuri?" with "Mamaanapikachakula." among the options.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T2_HATI_NADHIFU_HERUFI_.H.help: Put a finger space after every word.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T2_HATI_NADHIFU_HERUFI_.H.feedback: Acha nafasi ya kidole kati ya neno na neno.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T2_HATI_NADHIFU_HERUFI_.H.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUANDI.T2_HATI_NADHIFU_HERUFI_.H.error: Turns b and d (or p and q) round: dada written "baba" or "bada".
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T2_HATI_NADHIFU_HERUFI_.H.cause: Mirror letters are common in early writing; the child has not fixed the direction.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T2_HATI_NADHIFU_HERUFI_.H.reveals: The question "Andika neno "dada"." with "bada" among the options.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T2_HATI_NADHIFU_HERUFI_.H.help: Teach d as "c then a tall line"; trace it in sand.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T2_HATI_NADHIFU_HERUFI_.H.feedback: Herufi d huanza kama c, kisha mstari mrefu.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T2_HATI_NADHIFU_HERUFI_.H.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUANDI.T2_HATI_NADHIFU_HERUFI_.H.error: Writes letters floating above the line or of mixed sizes, so the line goes up and down.

example.question: Maandishi nadhifu yanakaa wapi?
example.correct_answer: juu ya mstari, herufi zikiwa na ukubwa sawa

KISW.G1.KUANDI.T2_HATI_NADHIFU_HERUFI_.H.cause: The child writes fast and does not look at the line.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T2_HATI_NADHIFU_HERUFI_.H.reveals: The question "Maandishi nadhifu yanakaa wapi?" with "popote kwenye ukurasa" among the options.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T2_HATI_NADHIFU_HERUFI_.H.help: Trace the line with a finger first; every letter sits on it.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T2_HATI_NADHIFU_HERUFI_.H.feedback: Kila herufi ikae juu ya mstari.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T2_HATI_NADHIFU_HERUFI_.H.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.SARUFI.T2_UMOJA_NA_WINGI_WA_MA.U.error: Makes the plural with the prefix of another noun class (kitabu -> watabu).
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T2_UMOJA_NA_WINGI_WA_MA.U.cause: The child knows that wa- makes people plural and uses it for everything; the ngeli of the noun is not yet known.
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T2_UMOJA_NA_WINGI_WA_MA.U.reveals: The question "Wingi wa "kiti" ni?" with "witi" among the options.
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T2_UMOJA_NA_WINGI_WA_MA.U.help: Sort noun cards into ngeli families (m-wa, ki-vi, li-ma, n-n) and say each plural aloud.
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T2_UMOJA_NA_WINGI_WA_MA.U.feedback: Kila ngeli ina wingi wake: kitabu - vitabu, mtoto - watoto. (viti)
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T2_UMOJA_NA_WINGI_WA_MA.U.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.SARUFI.T2_UMOJA_NA_WINGI_WA_MA.U.error: Shows the plural only with a number word and leaves the noun singular (kitabu mbili).
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T2_UMOJA_NA_WINGI_WA_MA.U.cause: English and some first languages keep the noun and add a number; Kiswahili changes the noun and the number agrees.
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T2_UMOJA_NA_WINGI_WA_MA.U.reveals: The question "Wingi wa "mtoto mmoja" ni?" with "mtoto wawili" among the options.
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T2_UMOJA_NA_WINGI_WA_MA.U.help: Line up two books: the child says vitabu viwili; then three: vitabu vitatu.
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T2_UMOJA_NA_WINGI_WA_MA.U.feedback: Nomino hubadilika pia: vitabu viwili. (watoto wawili)
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T2_UMOJA_NA_WINGI_WA_MA.U.source: mother-tongue sound interference common in Kenyan classrooms; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.SARUFI.T2_UMOJA_NA_WINGI_WA_MA.U.error: Takes the plural form for the singular (miti for one tree, vitabu for one book).
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T2_UMOJA_NA_WINGI_WA_MA.U.cause: The child heard the plural more often (a tree is usually among trees) and learnt it as the name.
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T2_UMOJA_NA_WINGI_WA_MA.U.reveals: The question "Ni lipi ni umoja?" with "vikombe" among the options.
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T2_UMOJA_NA_WINGI_WA_MA.U.help: Hold one object, then many; the child names each.
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T2_UMOJA_NA_WINGI_WA_MA.U.feedback: Kimoja ni kitabu; vingi ni vitabu. (kikombe)
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T2_UMOJA_NA_WINGI_WA_MA.U.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.SARUFI.T2_UMOJA_NA_WINGI_WA_MA.U.error: Gives a noun of the n-n class a plural prefix (nyumba -> manyumba), or changes an irregular noun wrongly (jicho -> majicho).
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T2_UMOJA_NA_WINGI_WA_MA.U.cause: The child expects every plural to look different; n-n nouns stay the same and some li-ma nouns change their stem.
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T2_UMOJA_NA_WINGI_WA_MA.U.reveals: The question "Wingi wa "kalamu" ni?" with "makalamu" among the options.
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T2_UMOJA_NA_WINGI_WA_MA.U.help: Keep a short list of the same-in-both nouns (nyumba, ndizi, kalamu) and the irregular ones (jicho - macho, jino - meno).
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T2_UMOJA_NA_WINGI_WA_MA.U.feedback: Baadhi ya nomino hazibadiliki, na baadhi hubadilika kwa njia yake. (kalamu)
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T2_UMOJA_NA_WINGI_WA_MA.U.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T3_MANENO_YA_ADABU_NA_H.H.error: Says samahani when someone else is hurt by accident, where pole (sympathy) is meant.

example.question: Rafiki ameanguka mwenyewe uwanjani. Unamwambia nini?

KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T3_MANENO_YA_ADABU_NA_H.H.cause: English "sorry" covers both apology and sympathy; Kiswahili separates them: samahani when I did wrong, pole when you suffer.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T3_MANENO_YA_ADABU_NA_H.H.reveals: The question "Rafiki ameanguka mwenyewe uwanjani. Unamwambia nini?" with "Samahani" among the options.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T3_MANENO_YA_ADABU_NA_H.H.help: Two pictures: I stepped on your foot (samahani); you fell by yourself (pole). The child names each.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T3_MANENO_YA_ADABU_NA_H.H.feedback: Pole ni ya kumhurumia aliyeumia; samahani ni ya kuomba msamaha ukikosea.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T3_MANENO_YA_ADABU_NA_H.H.source: English or mother-tongue interference on Kiswahili; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

example.question: Ulimpa rafiki kalamu, akasema "Asante." Unajibu nini?

KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T3_MANENO_YA_ADABU_NA_H.H.cause: The child echoes the polite word he has just heard.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T3_MANENO_YA_ADABU_NA_H.H.reveals: The question "Ulimpa rafiki kalamu, akasema "Asante." Unajibu nini?" with "Asante" among the options.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T3_MANENO_YA_ADABU_NA_H.H.help: Practise the pair with two children: one gives, one thanks, the giver answers Karibu.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T3_MANENO_YA_ADABU_NA_H.H.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T3_MANENO_YA_ADABU_NA_H.H.error: Asks with a bare command (Nipe maji!) without tafadhali or naomba.

example.question: Unataka maji kutoka kwa mama. Unasemaje?

KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T3_MANENO_YA_ADABU_NA_H.H.cause: At home and in play the child hears short commands and copies them to adults.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T3_MANENO_YA_ADABU_NA_H.H.reveals: The question "Unataka maji kutoka kwa mama. Unasemaje?" with "Nipe maji!" among the options.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T3_MANENO_YA_ADABU_NA_H.H.help: Say both versions; the child says which one makes mama want to help.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T3_MANENO_YA_ADABU_NA_H.H.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T3_MANENO_YA_ADABU_NA_H.H.error: Calls an adult by the bare first name without a title (Mwalimu, Mama, Baba, Bi., Bw.).

example.question: Unamwita mwalimu wako, Bi. Akinyi. Unasemaje?

KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T3_MANENO_YA_ADABU_NA_H.H.cause: Children call each other by name and carry the habit to adults.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T3_MANENO_YA_ADABU_NA_H.H.reveals: The question "Unamwita mwalimu wako, Bi. Akinyi. Unasemaje?" with "Akinyi, njoo!" among the options.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T3_MANENO_YA_ADABU_NA_H.H.help: Make title cards (Mwalimu, Mama, Babu, Daktari); the child puts one before each name.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T3_MANENO_YA_ADABU_NA_H.H.feedback: Mtu mzima huitwa kwa heshima: Mwalimu, Mama, Babu.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T3_MANENO_YA_ADABU_NA_H.H.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T3_MANENO_YA_ADABU_NA_H.H.cause: The child echoes the word, as with greetings.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T3_MANENO_YA_ADABU_NA_H.H.reveals: The question "Rafiki anakuambia "Pole kwa kuumia." Unajibu?" with "Pole" among the options.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T3_MANENO_YA_ADABU_NA_H.H.help: Act it: one child is hurt, the other says pole, the hurt one says asante.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T3_MANENO_YA_ADABU_NA_H.H.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T3_KUSOMA_KWA_UFAHAMU.UFA.error: Reads every word aloud but cannot say what the passage was about.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T3_KUSOMA_KWA_UFAHAMU.UFA.cause: All the child's effort goes into sounding out the words; nobody has asked him what the sentences said.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T3_KUSOMA_KWA_UFAHAMU.UFA.reveals: The question "Umesoma kifungu. Kinahusu nini?" with "Sijui, nilikuwa nikisoma maneno tu." among the options.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T3_KUSOMA_KWA_UFAHAMU.UFA.help: After each sentence stop and ask "Sentensi hii imesema nini?" before reading on.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T3_KUSOMA_KWA_UFAHAMU.UFA.feedback: Soma tena polepole na ufikirie maana: Kifungu kinahusu kuku wa Juma.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T3_KUSOMA_KWA_UFAHAMU.UFA.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T3_KUSOMA_KWA_UFAHAMU.UFA.error: Gives "watano" the meaning of a word that looks or sounds like it.

example.question: Soma: "Juma ana kuku watano. Kuku wawili ni weupe. Kuku watatu ni weusi. Juma anawapenda kuku wake." Neno "watano" lina maana gani?

KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T3_KUSOMA_KWA_UFAHAMU.UFA.cause: The child matches the word to a known one by its look instead of reading the sentence around it.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T3_KUSOMA_KWA_UFAHAMU.UFA.reveals: The question "Soma: "Juma ana kuku watano. Kuku wawili ni weupe. Kuku watatu ni weusi. Juma anawapenda kuku wake." Neno "watano" lina maana gani?" with "watoto" among the options.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T3_KUSOMA_KWA_UFAHAMU.UFA.help: Cover the word; the child says what word would fit the sentence, then uncovers it.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T3_KUSOMA_KWA_UFAHAMU.UFA.feedback: Katika kifungu, "watano" ni idadi ya tano.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T3_KUSOMA_KWA_UFAHAMU.UFA.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T3_KUSOMA_KWA_UFAHAMU.UFA.error: Gives one detail of the passage as its message.

example.question: Ujumbe wa kifungu ni upi?
example.correct_answer: Juma ana kuku watano na anawapenda.

KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T3_KUSOMA_KWA_UFAHAMU.UFA.cause: The detail is what the child remembers best; he has not been asked what the writer wants us to know.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T3_KUSOMA_KWA_UFAHAMU.UFA.reveals: The question "Ujumbe wa kifungu ni upi?" with "Kuku wawili ni weupe." among the options.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T3_KUSOMA_KWA_UFAHAMU.UFA.help: Ask two questions side by side: "Nini kilitokea?" and "Kifungu kinatuambia nini?"
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T3_KUSOMA_KWA_UFAHAMU.UFA.feedback: Hilo ni tukio moja. Ujumbe ni: Juma ana kuku watano na anawapenda.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T3_KUSOMA_KWA_UFAHAMU.UFA.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T3_KUSOMA_KWA_UFAHAMU.UFA.error: Answers from his own life instead of from the passage.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T3_KUSOMA_KWA_UFAHAMU.UFA.cause: The child links the question to what he knows from home and does not check the text.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T3_KUSOMA_KWA_UFAHAMU.UFA.reveals: The question "Juma ana kuku wangapi?" with "Sisi tuna kuku kumi." among the options.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T3_KUSOMA_KWA_UFAHAMU.UFA.help: Ask the child to point at the line in the passage that gives the answer.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T3_KUSOMA_KWA_UFAHAMU.UFA.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUANDI.T3_HATI_NADHIFU_HERUFI_.H.error: Writes the tall small letters (b, d, h, k, l) short, so h looks like n.

example.question: Andika neno "habari". Ni lipi limeandikwa vizuri?

KISW.G1.KUANDI.T3_HATI_NADHIFU_HERUFI_.H.cause: The child does not use the lines of the book: tall letters must reach the top line.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T3_HATI_NADHIFU_HERUFI_.H.reveals: The question "Andika neno "habari". Ni lipi limeandikwa vizuri?" with "nabari" among the options.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T3_HATI_NADHIFU_HERUFI_.H.help: Write on three-line paper; the child colours the part of h that goes up.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T3_HATI_NADHIFU_HERUFI_.H.feedback: Herufi h, k, l, b, d hupanda juu ya mstari wa kati.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T3_HATI_NADHIFU_HERUFI_.H.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUANDI.T3_HATI_NADHIFU_HERUFI_.H.error: Writes some small letters as big as capitals (kiti written kiTi or KITI).

example.question: Ni neno lipi limeandikwa kwa herufi ndogo vizuri?

KISW.G1.KUANDI.T3_HATI_NADHIFU_HERUFI_.H.cause: Capitals were learnt first in pre-primary and feel safer to write.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T3_HATI_NADHIFU_HERUFI_.H.reveals: The question "Ni neno lipi limeandikwa kwa herufi ndogo vizuri?" with "KITI" among the options.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T3_HATI_NADHIFU_HERUFI_.H.help: Compare k/K, s/S, t/T on cards; the child picks the small one for the middle of a word.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T3_HATI_NADHIFU_HERUFI_.H.feedback: Ndani ya neno tumia herufi ndogo.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T3_HATI_NADHIFU_HERUFI_.H.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUANDI.T3_HATI_NADHIFU_HERUFI_.H.cause: Spoken Kiswahili runs words together; the child writes the stream as he hears it.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T3_HATI_NADHIFU_HERUFI_.H.reveals: The question "Ni lipi limeandikwa vizuri?" with "Mamaanapikachakula." among the options.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T3_HATI_NADHIFU_HERUFI_.H.help: Put a finger space after every word.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T3_HATI_NADHIFU_HERUFI_.H.feedback: Acha nafasi ya kidole kati ya neno na neno.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T3_HATI_NADHIFU_HERUFI_.H.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUANDI.T3_HATI_NADHIFU_HERUFI_.H.error: Turns b and d (or p and q) round: dada written "baba" or "bada".
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T3_HATI_NADHIFU_HERUFI_.H.cause: Mirror letters are common in early writing; the child has not fixed the direction.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T3_HATI_NADHIFU_HERUFI_.H.reveals: The question "Andika neno "dada"." with "bada" among the options.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T3_HATI_NADHIFU_HERUFI_.H.help: Teach d as "c then a tall line"; trace it in sand.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T3_HATI_NADHIFU_HERUFI_.H.feedback: Herufi d huanza kama c, kisha mstari mrefu.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T3_HATI_NADHIFU_HERUFI_.H.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUANDI.T3_HATI_NADHIFU_HERUFI_.H.error: Writes letters floating above the line or of mixed sizes, so the line goes up and down.

example.question: Maandishi nadhifu yanakaa wapi?
example.correct_answer: juu ya mstari, herufi zikiwa na ukubwa sawa

KISW.G1.KUANDI.T3_HATI_NADHIFU_HERUFI_.H.cause: The child writes fast and does not look at the line.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T3_HATI_NADHIFU_HERUFI_.H.reveals: The question "Maandishi nadhifu yanakaa wapi?" with "popote kwenye ukurasa" among the options.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T3_HATI_NADHIFU_HERUFI_.H.help: Trace the line with a finger first; every letter sits on it.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T3_HATI_NADHIFU_HERUFI_.H.feedback: Kila herufi ikae juu ya mstari.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T3_HATI_NADHIFU_HERUFI_.H.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.SARUFI.T3_MATUMIZI_YA_HUYU_NA_.V.error: Uses the people word (huyu, yule) for a thing (kiti huyu).
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T3_MATUMIZI_YA_HUYU_NA_.V.cause: Huyu was the first pointing word learnt; the child uses it for anything.
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T3_MATUMIZI_YA_HUYU_NA_.V.reveals: The question "Jaza: Kiti ___ ni changu." with "huyu" among the options.
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T3_MATUMIZI_YA_HUYU_NA_.V.help: Point at a child (huyu) and at a chair (hiki); then sort pictures by the pointing word they take.
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T3_MATUMIZI_YA_HUYU_NA_.V.feedback: Kitu cha ngeli ya ki-vi huonyeshwa kwa hiki; mtu huonyeshwa kwa huyu. (hiki)
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T3_MATUMIZI_YA_HUYU_NA_.V.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.SARUFI.T3_MATUMIZI_YA_HUYU_NA_.V.error: Uses the one-thing pointing word with a plural noun (watoto huyu).
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T3_MATUMIZI_YA_HUYU_NA_.V.cause: The child changes the noun but not the pointing word.
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T3_MATUMIZI_YA_HUYU_NA_.V.reveals: The question "Jaza: Watoto ___ ni wanafunzi." with "huyu" among the options.
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T3_MATUMIZI_YA_HUYU_NA_.V.help: Pair the forms on cards: huyu-hawa, yule-wale, hiki-hivi, hili-haya.
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T3_MATUMIZI_YA_HUYU_NA_.V.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.SARUFI.T3_MATUMIZI_YA_HUYU_NA_.V.error: Uses hii for every noun (kitabu hii, mtoto hii), as in town Kiswahili.
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T3_MATUMIZI_YA_HUYU_NA_.V.cause: Hii is the pointing word heard most in town speech, where the noun class is dropped.
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T3_MATUMIZI_YA_HUYU_NA_.V.reveals: The question "Jaza: Mtoto ___ ni dada yangu." with "hii" among the options.
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T3_MATUMIZI_YA_HUYU_NA_.V.help: Read pairs aloud: kitabu hiki, mtoto huyu, nyumba hii; the child hears the match.
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T3_MATUMIZI_YA_HUYU_NA_.V.feedback: Kitabu hiki; mtoto huyu; nyumba hii. (huyu)
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T3_MATUMIZI_YA_HUYU_NA_.V.source: mother-tongue sound interference common in Kenyan classrooms; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.SARUFI.T3_MATUMIZI_YA_HUYU_NA_.V.error: Takes the plural form for the singular (miti for one tree, vitabu for one book).

example.question: Ni lipi ni la mtu mmoja?

KISW.G1.SARUFI.T3_MATUMIZI_YA_HUYU_NA_.V.cause: The child heard the plural more often (a tree is usually among trees) and learnt it as the name.
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T3_MATUMIZI_YA_HUYU_NA_.V.reveals: The question "Ni lipi ni la mtu mmoja?" with "hawa" among the options.
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T3_MATUMIZI_YA_HUYU_NA_.V.help: Hold one object, then many; the child names each.
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T3_MATUMIZI_YA_HUYU_NA_.V.feedback: Kimoja ni kitabu; vingi ni vitabu. (huyu)
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T3_MATUMIZI_YA_HUYU_NA_.V.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

example.question: Mwalimu anasema "wewe". Neno lipi limetamkwa vizuri?

KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T4_MATAMSHI_BORA_SAUTI_.M.cause: Many Kenyan first languages have no /e/, or do not separate it from /i/; the child puts in the home sound.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T4_MATAMSHI_BORA_SAUTI_.M.reveals: The question "Mwalimu anasema "wewe". Neno lipi limetamkwa vizuri?" with "wiwi" among the options.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T4_MATAMSHI_BORA_SAUTI_.M.help: Say the two side by side, slowly, watching the mouth; the child holds up a card for the sound he hears.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T4_MATAMSHI_BORA_SAUTI_.M.source: mother-tongue sound interference common in Kenyan classrooms; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T4_MATAMSHI_BORA_SAUTI_.M.cause: /o/ and /u/ are close; a first language with only one of them puts that one in both places.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T4_MATAMSHI_BORA_SAUTI_.M.reveals: The question "Neno lipi limetamkwa vizuri?" with "nunu" among the options.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T4_MATAMSHI_BORA_SAUTI_.M.help: Contrast the two with a mirror and a hand before the mouth; the child says which he hears.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T4_MATAMSHI_BORA_SAUTI_.M.source: mother-tongue sound interference common in Kenyan classrooms; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T4_MATAMSHI_BORA_SAUTI_.M.error: Splits "nane" by letters rather than by syllables (each Kiswahili syllable ends in a vowel).
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T4_MATAMSHI_BORA_SAUTI_.M.cause: The child has learnt letters one by one and has not been shown that a syllable is a sound that ends in a vowel.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T4_MATAMSHI_BORA_SAUTI_.M.reveals: The question "Neno "nane" lina silabi zipi?" with "n-a-n-e" among the options.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T4_MATAMSHI_BORA_SAUTI_.M.help: Clap the word: one clap per vowel; the consonants go with the vowel after them.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T4_MATAMSHI_BORA_SAUTI_.M.feedback: Kila silabi ya Kiswahili huishia kwa irabu: na-ne.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T4_MATAMSHI_BORA_SAUTI_.M.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T4_MATAMSHI_BORA_SAUTI_.M.error: Says the English letter name instead of the Kiswahili sound (/e/ as "ii"), so the syllable cannot be built.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T4_MATAMSHI_BORA_SAUTI_.M.cause: English letter names are taught alongside and the child brings them to Kiswahili; a syllable is built from sounds, not names.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T4_MATAMSHI_BORA_SAUTI_.M.reveals: The question "Sauti ya herufi "e" ni ipi?" with "ii" among the options.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T4_MATAMSHI_BORA_SAUTI_.M.help: Say the sound alone, short (/e/), then join it to a vowel: ea, ee, ei.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T4_MATAMSHI_BORA_SAUTI_.M.source: English or mother-tongue interference on Kiswahili; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T4_MATAMSHI_BORA_SAUTI_.M.error: Picks a word with no target sound when asked for one that has it.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T4_MATAMSHI_BORA_SAUTI_.M.cause: The child looks at the first letter or the picture, not at the sound.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T4_MATAMSHI_BORA_SAUTI_.M.reveals: The question "Ni neno lipi lina sauti /n/, /o/, /w/, /e/, /i/, /h/?" with "mama" among the options.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T4_MATAMSHI_BORA_SAUTI_.M.help: Underline the target sound in each word on the card before choosing.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T4_MATAMSHI_BORA_SAUTI_.M.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T4_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA.KUS.error: Reads the target word wrongly: "wewe" as "wiwi".
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T4_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA.KUS.cause: The child reads the letters with the sounds of his first language, or adds a vowel to break the cluster.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T4_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA.KUS.reveals: The question "Neno "wewe" linasomwa vipi?" with "wiwi" among the options.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T4_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA.KUS.help: Pick out the target words before reading; practise them on cards, then read the passage.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T4_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA.KUS.source: mother-tongue sound interference common in Kenyan classrooms; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T4_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA.KUS.error: Reads word by word or syllable by syllable, so the sentence has no meaning when heard.

example.question: Ni usomaji upi ni wa ufasaha: "Leo ni siku ya Jumanne."?

KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T4_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA.KUS.cause: The child is still decoding each word; he has not yet read a group of words as one piece.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T4_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA.KUS.reveals: The question "Ni usomaji upi ni wa ufasaha: "Leo ni siku ya Jumanne."?" with "Leo ... ni ... siku ... ya ... Jumanne." among the options.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T4_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA.KUS.help: Echo reading: the teacher reads a phrase, the child repeats it in one breath.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T4_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA.KUS.feedback: Soma maneno kwa pamoja kama unavyozungumza.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T4_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA.KUS.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T4_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA.KUS.error: Reads so softly (or so loudly, shouting) that the class cannot follow.

example.question: Unaposoma mbele ya darasa, sauti yako inafaa kuwa vipi?
example.wrong_answer: ya chini ili nisikosee mbele ya wenzangu
example.correct_answer: ya kusikika na wote darasani, bila kupiga kelele

KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T4_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA.KUS.cause: Shyness, or the belief that reading well means reading loud.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T4_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA.KUS.reveals: The question "Unaposoma mbele ya darasa, sauti yako inafaa kuwa vipi?" with "ya chini ili nisikosee mbele ya wenzangu" among the options.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T4_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA.KUS.help: Stand the reader at the front and a listener at the back: the listener raises a hand when he hears every word.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T4_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA.KUS.feedback: Soma kwa sauti inayosikika na wote, bila kupiga kelele.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T4_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA.KUS.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T4_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA.KUS.error: Reads as fast as possible and thinks the fastest reader is the best.

example.question: Kasi ifaayo ya kusoma kifungu ni ipi?
example.correct_answer: kasi ya kuzungumza, karibu maneno 15 kwa dakika

KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T4_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA.KUS.cause: Reading races in class reward speed; nobody asked whether the listeners understood.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T4_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA.KUS.reveals: The question "Kasi ifaayo ya kusoma kifungu ni ipi?" with "haraka iwezekanavyo" among the options.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T4_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA.KUS.help: Time two readings, one very fast and one at speaking pace; the listeners answer one question after each.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T4_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA.KUS.feedback: Kasi ifaayo ni ya kuzungumza: si haraka mno, si polepole mno.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T4_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA.KUS.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T4_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA.KUS.error: Reads a question in the flat voice of a statement and runs on through the koma and kikomo.

example.question: Sentensi "Je, wewe uko nyumbani?" inasomwa vipi?
example.wrong_answer: kwa sauti ileile ya sentensi ya kawaida
example.correct_answer: sauti hupanda mwishoni kwa sababu ni swali

KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T4_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA.KUS.cause: The child looks at the words and not at the marks.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T4_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA.KUS.reveals: The question "Sentensi "Je, wewe uko nyumbani?" inasomwa vipi?" with "kwa sauti ileile ya sentensi ya kawaida" among the options.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T4_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA.KUS.help: Read the same words three ways (. ? !); the child points at the mark that fits each reading; clap at each kikomo.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T4_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA.KUS.feedback: Kiulizi (?) hupandisha sauti mwishoni; simama kidogo kwenye koma na kikomo.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T4_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA.KUS.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUANDI.T4_HATI_NADHIFU.KUUNGANIS.error: Leaves a gap between every letter of a word (m a m a).
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T4_HATI_NADHIFU.KUUNGANIS.cause: The child learnt each letter alone and keeps a space after it.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T4_HATI_NADHIFU.KUUNGANIS.reveals: The question "Ni lipi limeandikwa vizuri?" with "m a m a" among the options.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T4_HATI_NADHIFU.KUUNGANIS.help: Write the syllable as one block (ma), then put two blocks together (mama), close.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T4_HATI_NADHIFU.KUUNGANIS.feedback: Herufi za neno moja hukaa karibu: mama.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T4_HATI_NADHIFU.KUUNGANIS.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUANDI.T4_HATI_NADHIFU.KUUNGANIS.error: Joins the syllables in the wrong order (ta + tu written tuta for tatu).
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T4_HATI_NADHIFU.KUUNGANIS.cause: The child hears both syllables but writes the one he remembers best first.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T4_HATI_NADHIFU.KUUNGANIS.reveals: The question "Unganisha silabi: ta + tu" with "tuta" among the options.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T4_HATI_NADHIFU.KUUNGANIS.help: Clap the word and write one syllable per clap, in order, saying each.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T4_HATI_NADHIFU.KUUNGANIS.feedback: Andika silabi kwa mpangilio unaozisikia: ta-tu.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T4_HATI_NADHIFU.KUUNGANIS.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUANDI.T4_HATI_NADHIFU.KUUNGANIS.error: Leaves out the vowel of a syllable (mm for mama, kk for kaka).
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T4_HATI_NADHIFU.KUUNGANIS.cause: The child writes the consonants he hears most strongly; the vowel ending each syllable is missed.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T4_HATI_NADHIFU.KUUNGANIS.reveals: The question "Unganisha silabi: ka + ka" with "kk" among the options.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T4_HATI_NADHIFU.KUUNGANIS.help: Every syllable ends in a vowel: say the vowel long (kaaa) and write it.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T4_HATI_NADHIFU.KUUNGANIS.feedback: Kila silabi huishia kwa irabu: ka-ka.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T4_HATI_NADHIFU.KUUNGANIS.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUANDI.T4_HATI_NADHIFU.KUUNGANIS.error: Writes each syllable on a new line, or one above the other.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T4_HATI_NADHIFU.KUUNGANIS.cause: Syllable cards were stacked in class and the child copies the stack.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T4_HATI_NADHIFU.KUUNGANIS.reveals: The question "Neno "baba" liandikwe vipi?" with "ba juu, ba chini" among the options.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T4_HATI_NADHIFU.KUUNGANIS.help: Lay the syllable cards side by side on the desk before writing.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T4_HATI_NADHIFU.KUUNGANIS.feedback: Silabi za neno moja hukaa kwenye mstari mmoja.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T4_HATI_NADHIFU.KUUNGANIS.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.SARUFI.T4_UMOJA_NA_WINGI_WA_MA.U.error: Makes the plural with the prefix of another noun class (kitabu -> watabu).
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T4_UMOJA_NA_WINGI_WA_MA.U.cause: The child knows that wa- makes people plural and uses it for everything; the ngeli of the noun is not yet known.
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T4_UMOJA_NA_WINGI_WA_MA.U.reveals: The question "Wingi wa "mti" ni?" with "viti" among the options.
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T4_UMOJA_NA_WINGI_WA_MA.U.help: Sort noun cards into ngeli families (m-wa, ki-vi, li-ma, n-n) and say each plural aloud.
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T4_UMOJA_NA_WINGI_WA_MA.U.feedback: Kila ngeli ina wingi wake: kitabu - vitabu, mtoto - watoto. (miti)
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T4_UMOJA_NA_WINGI_WA_MA.U.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.SARUFI.T4_UMOJA_NA_WINGI_WA_MA.U.error: Gives a noun of the n-n class a plural prefix (nyumba -> manyumba), or changes an irregular noun wrongly (jicho -> majicho).
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T4_UMOJA_NA_WINGI_WA_MA.U.cause: The child expects every plural to look different; n-n nouns stay the same and some li-ma nouns change their stem.
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T4_UMOJA_NA_WINGI_WA_MA.U.reveals: The question "Wingi wa "jicho" ni?" with "majicho" among the options.
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T4_UMOJA_NA_WINGI_WA_MA.U.help: Keep a short list of the same-in-both nouns (nyumba, ndizi, kalamu) and the irregular ones (jicho - macho, jino - meno).
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T4_UMOJA_NA_WINGI_WA_MA.U.feedback: Baadhi ya nomino hazibadiliki, na baadhi hubadilika kwa njia yake. (macho)
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T4_UMOJA_NA_WINGI_WA_MA.U.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.SARUFI.T4_UMOJA_NA_WINGI_WA_MA.U.error: Shows the plural only with a number word and leaves the noun singular (kitabu mbili).
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T4_UMOJA_NA_WINGI_WA_MA.U.cause: English and some first languages keep the noun and add a number; Kiswahili changes the noun and the number agrees.
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T4_UMOJA_NA_WINGI_WA_MA.U.reveals: The question "Wingi wa "yai moja" ni?" with "yai mbili" among the options.
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T4_UMOJA_NA_WINGI_WA_MA.U.help: Line up two books: the child says vitabu viwili; then three: vitabu vitatu.
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T4_UMOJA_NA_WINGI_WA_MA.U.feedback: Nomino hubadilika pia: vitabu viwili. (mayai mawili)
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T4_UMOJA_NA_WINGI_WA_MA.U.source: mother-tongue sound interference common in Kenyan classrooms; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.SARUFI.T4_UMOJA_NA_WINGI_WA_MA.U.error: Takes the plural form for the singular (miti for one tree, vitabu for one book).
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T4_UMOJA_NA_WINGI_WA_MA.U.cause: The child heard the plural more often (a tree is usually among trees) and learnt it as the name.
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T4_UMOJA_NA_WINGI_WA_MA.U.reveals: The question "Ni lipi ni umoja?" with "majani" among the options.
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T4_UMOJA_NA_WINGI_WA_MA.U.help: Hold one object, then many; the child names each.
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T4_UMOJA_NA_WINGI_WA_MA.U.feedback: Kimoja ni kitabu; vingi ni vitabu. (jani)
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T4_UMOJA_NA_WINGI_WA_MA.U.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T5_UFAHAMU_WA_KUSIKILIZ.U.error: Gives a detail of the passage as its message.

example.question: Ujumbe wa kifungu ulichosikiliza ni upi?

KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T5_UFAHAMU_WA_KUSIKILIZ.U.cause: The detail is the clearest thing the child remembers; he has not been asked what the passage teaches.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T5_UFAHAMU_WA_KUSIKILIZ.U.reveals: The question "Ujumbe wa kifungu ulichosikiliza ni upi?" with "Kamau alisahau chakula." among the options.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T5_UFAHAMU_WA_KUSIKILIZ.U.help: After listening, ask "Kifungu kinatufundisha nini?" and compare it with "Nini kilitokea?".
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T5_UFAHAMU_WA_KUSIKILIZ.U.feedback: Hilo ni tukio moja. Ujumbe ni: Tushiriki tulicho nacho na wenzetu.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T5_UFAHAMU_WA_KUSIKILIZ.U.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T5_UFAHAMU_WA_KUSIKILIZ.U.error: Gives "kushiriki" the meaning of a word that sounds like it.

example.question: Neno "kushiriki" katika kifungu lina maana gani?

KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T5_UFAHAMU_WA_KUSIKILIZ.U.cause: The child matches the sound of the word to one he knows instead of listening to the sentence around it.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T5_UFAHAMU_WA_KUSIKILIZ.U.reveals: The question "Neno "kushiriki" katika kifungu lina maana gani?" with "kushinda" among the options.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T5_UFAHAMU_WA_KUSIKILIZ.U.help: Replay the sentence; the child tries each meaning in it and keeps the one that makes sense.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T5_UFAHAMU_WA_KUSIKILIZ.U.feedback: Katika kifungu, "kushiriki" ni kugawana kitu na mwenzako.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T5_UFAHAMU_WA_KUSIKILIZ.U.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T5_UFAHAMU_WA_KUSIKILIZ.U.error: Makes a "sentence" that only repeats the word and shows no meaning (kushiriki ni kushiriki).

example.question: Ni sentensi ipi inaonyesha maana ya "kushiriki"?

KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T5_UFAHAMU_WA_KUSIKILIZ.U.cause: The child thinks any sentence with the word in it is enough.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T5_UFAHAMU_WA_KUSIKILIZ.U.reveals: The question "Ni sentensi ipi inaonyesha maana ya "kushiriki"?" with "Kushiriki ni kushiriki." among the options.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T5_UFAHAMU_WA_KUSIKILIZ.U.help: Ask: if your friend did not know the word, would your sentence tell him what it means?
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T5_UFAHAMU_WA_KUSIKILIZ.U.feedback: Sentensi nzuri inaonyesha maana ya neno.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T5_UFAHAMU_WA_KUSIKILIZ.U.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T5_UFAHAMU_WA_KUSIKILIZ.U.error: Retells the events out of order.

example.question: Panga matukio ya kifungu kama yalivyotokea.
example.wrong_answer: Walikula pamoja, Kamau alisahau chakula, Otieno alimgawia
example.correct_answer: Kamau alisahau chakula, Otieno alimgawia, walikula pamoja

KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T5_UFAHAMU_WA_KUSIKILIZ.U.cause: The child remembers the most exciting event and tells it first.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T5_UFAHAMU_WA_KUSIKILIZ.U.reveals: The question "Panga matukio ya kifungu kama yalivyotokea." with "Walikula pamoja, Kamau alisahau chakula, Otieno alimgawia" among the options.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T5_UFAHAMU_WA_KUSIKILIZ.U.help: Three picture cards of the events; the child lays them left to right and retells with kwanza, kisha, mwishowe.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T5_UFAHAMU_WA_KUSIKILIZ.U.feedback: Matukio yalifuatana hivi: Kamau alisahau chakula, Otieno alimgawia, walikula pamoja.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T5_UFAHAMU_WA_KUSIKILIZ.U.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T5_UFAHAMU_WA_KUSIKILIZ.U.error: Adds events that were not in the passage when retelling.

example.question: Unaposimulia upya, unaongeza mambo ambayo hayakuwa kwenye kifungu?

KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T5_UFAHAMU_WA_KUSIKILIZ.U.cause: Retelling is taken as storytelling: the child invents to make it longer.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T5_UFAHAMU_WA_KUSIKILIZ.U.reveals: The question "Unaposimulia upya, unaongeza mambo ambayo hayakuwa kwenye kifungu?" with "ndiyo, ili hadithi iwe tamu" among the options.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T5_UFAHAMU_WA_KUSIKILIZ.U.help: After the retelling, the class checks each event: was it in the passage? Thumbs up or down.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T5_UFAHAMU_WA_KUSIKILIZ.U.feedback: Kusimulia upya ni kusema yaliyokuwa kwenye kifungu tu.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T5_UFAHAMU_WA_KUSIKILIZ.U.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T5_KUSOMA_KWA_UFAHAMU_K.U.error: Reads every word aloud but cannot say what the passage was about.

example.question: Umesoma kifungu. Kinahusu nini?
example.correct_answer: Kifungu kinahusu Akinyi na rafiki yake Wanjiku.

KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T5_KUSOMA_KWA_UFAHAMU_K.U.cause: All the child's effort goes into sounding out the words; nobody has asked him what the sentences said.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T5_KUSOMA_KWA_UFAHAMU_K.U.reveals: The question "Umesoma kifungu. Kinahusu nini?" with "Sijui, nilikuwa nikisoma maneno tu." among the options.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T5_KUSOMA_KWA_UFAHAMU_K.U.help: After each sentence stop and ask "Sentensi hii imesema nini?" before reading on.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T5_KUSOMA_KWA_UFAHAMU_K.U.feedback: Soma tena polepole na ufikirie maana: Kifungu kinahusu Akinyi na rafiki yake Wanjiku.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T5_KUSOMA_KWA_UFAHAMU_K.U.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T5_KUSOMA_KWA_UFAHAMU_K.U.error: Gives "tunasaidiana" the meaning of a word that looks or sounds like it.

example.question: Soma: "Mimi ni Akinyi. Nina rafiki anayeitwa Wanjiku. Tunacheza pamoja shuleni. Tunasaidiana kila siku." Neno "tunasaidiana" lina maana gani?

KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T5_KUSOMA_KWA_UFAHAMU_K.U.cause: The child matches the word to a known one by its look instead of reading the sentence around it.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T5_KUSOMA_KWA_UFAHAMU_K.U.reveals: The question "Soma: "Mimi ni Akinyi. Nina rafiki anayeitwa Wanjiku. Tunacheza pamoja shuleni. Tunasaidiana kila siku." Neno "tunasaidiana" lina maana gani?" with "tunasalimiana" among the options.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T5_KUSOMA_KWA_UFAHAMU_K.U.help: Cover the word; the child says what word would fit the sentence, then uncovers it.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T5_KUSOMA_KWA_UFAHAMU_K.U.feedback: Katika kifungu, "tunasaidiana" ni kila mmoja anamsaidia mwenzake.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T5_KUSOMA_KWA_UFAHAMU_K.U.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T5_KUSOMA_KWA_UFAHAMU_K.U.error: Gives one detail of the passage as its message.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T5_KUSOMA_KWA_UFAHAMU_K.U.cause: The detail is what the child remembers best; he has not been asked what the writer wants us to know.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T5_KUSOMA_KWA_UFAHAMU_K.U.reveals: The question "Ujumbe wa kifungu ni upi?" with "Akinyi yuko shuleni." among the options.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T5_KUSOMA_KWA_UFAHAMU_K.U.help: Ask two questions side by side: "Nini kilitokea?" and "Kifungu kinatuambia nini?"
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T5_KUSOMA_KWA_UFAHAMU_K.U.feedback: Hilo ni tukio moja. Ujumbe ni: Marafiki hucheza pamoja na kusaidiana.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T5_KUSOMA_KWA_UFAHAMU_K.U.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T5_KUSOMA_KWA_UFAHAMU_K.U.error: Answers from his own life instead of from the passage.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T5_KUSOMA_KWA_UFAHAMU_K.U.cause: The child links the question to what he knows from home and does not check the text.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T5_KUSOMA_KWA_UFAHAMU_K.U.reveals: The question "Rafiki wa Akinyi anaitwa nani?" with "Rafiki yangu ni Otieno." among the options.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T5_KUSOMA_KWA_UFAHAMU_K.U.help: Ask the child to point at the line in the passage that gives the answer.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T5_KUSOMA_KWA_UFAHAMU_K.U.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUANDI.T5_MATUMIZI_YA_KIKOMO.ALA.error: Runs sentences together with no kikomo.

example.question: Ni lipi limeandikwa vizuri?
example.wrong_answer: Juma alienda shuleni alisoma vizuri alirudi nyumbani
example.correct_answer: Juma alienda shuleni. Alisoma vizuri. Alirudi nyumbani.

KISW.G1.KUANDI.T5_MATUMIZI_YA_KIKOMO.ALA.cause: The child writes as he speaks, one long breath.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T5_MATUMIZI_YA_KIKOMO.ALA.reveals: The question "Ni lipi limeandikwa vizuri?" with "Juma alienda shuleni alisoma vizuri alirudi nyumbani" among the options.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T5_MATUMIZI_YA_KIKOMO.ALA.help: Read the writing aloud; where the breath stops, put a kikomo.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T5_MATUMIZI_YA_KIKOMO.ALA.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUANDI.T5_MATUMIZI_YA_KIKOMO.ALA.error: Puts a kikomo at the end of every line of writing, not at the end of the sentence.

example.question: Kikomo huwekwa wapi?
example.wrong_answer: mwishoni mwa kila mstari wa daftari

KISW.G1.KUANDI.T5_MATUMIZI_YA_KIKOMO.ALA.cause: The line of the book looks like the end of a sentence.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T5_MATUMIZI_YA_KIKOMO.ALA.reveals: The question "Kikomo huwekwa wapi?" with "mwishoni mwa kila mstari wa daftari" among the options.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T5_MATUMIZI_YA_KIKOMO.ALA.help: Write one sentence that runs over two lines; the child finds where it really ends.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T5_MATUMIZI_YA_KIKOMO.ALA.feedback: Kikomo huwekwa sentensi inapoisha, si mstari.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T5_MATUMIZI_YA_KIKOMO.ALA.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUANDI.T5_MATUMIZI_YA_KIKOMO.ALA.error: Writes a small letter after a kikomo or kiulizi.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T5_MATUMIZI_YA_KIKOMO.ALA.cause: The child does not link the mark to the capital that follows it.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T5_MATUMIZI_YA_KIKOMO.ALA.reveals: The question "Ni lipi sahihi?" with "Mimi ni Amina. mama alifurahi." among the options.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T5_MATUMIZI_YA_KIKOMO.ALA.help: Every kikomo is a gate: the next word starts big.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T5_MATUMIZI_YA_KIKOMO.ALA.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUANDI.T5_MATUMIZI_YA_KIKOMO.ALA.error: Ends a question with a kikomo.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T5_MATUMIZI_YA_KIKOMO.ALA.cause: The child ends every sentence the same way.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T5_MATUMIZI_YA_KIKOMO.ALA.reveals: The question "Weka alama sahihi: Unaenda wapi" with "Unaenda wapi." among the options.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T5_MATUMIZI_YA_KIKOMO.ALA.help: Read the sentence aloud: if the voice rises and asks, it takes a kiulizi.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T5_MATUMIZI_YA_KIKOMO.ALA.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.SARUFI.T5_MATUMIZI_YA_ANGU_NA_.V.error: Uses the wrong noun-class form of the possessive (kitabu yangu for kitabu changu).
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T5_MATUMIZI_YA_ANGU_NA_.V.cause: Town Kiswahili uses yangu, yako, yake for every noun; the child has not seen the ngeli agreement.
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T5_MATUMIZI_YA_ANGU_NA_.V.reveals: The question "Jaza: Kitabu ___ (-angu) ni kipya." with "yangu" among the options.
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T5_MATUMIZI_YA_ANGU_NA_.V.help: Pair nouns and possessives by colour: kitabu changu, kiti chake, mtoto wangu.
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T5_MATUMIZI_YA_ANGU_NA_.V.feedback: Kitabu changu; kiti chake: kimilikishi hufuata ngeli. (changu)
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T5_MATUMIZI_YA_ANGU_NA_.V.source: mother-tongue sound interference common in Kenyan classrooms; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.SARUFI.T5_MATUMIZI_YA_ANGU_NA_.V.error: Leaves the possessive singular with a plural noun (vitabu changu).
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T5_MATUMIZI_YA_ANGU_NA_.V.cause: The child changes the noun and forgets the possessive.
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T5_MATUMIZI_YA_ANGU_NA_.V.reveals: The question "Jaza: Vitabu ___ (-angu) ni vipya." with "changu" among the options.
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T5_MATUMIZI_YA_ANGU_NA_.V.help: Change one object to many in front of the child; both words change.
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T5_MATUMIZI_YA_ANGU_NA_.V.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.SARUFI.T5_MATUMIZI_YA_ANGU_NA_.V.error: Uses the possessive of the wrong owner (-ake for something that is his own, -ake for many owners).

example.question: Mimi na wenzangu tuna darasa. Ni darasa ___.

KISW.G1.SARUFI.T5_MATUMIZI_YA_ANGU_NA_.V.cause: The child has not linked -angu, -ako, -ake, -etu, -enu, -ao to who owns the thing.
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T5_MATUMIZI_YA_ANGU_NA_.V.reveals: The question "Mimi na wenzangu tuna darasa. Ni darasa ___." with "langu" among the options.
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T5_MATUMIZI_YA_ANGU_NA_.V.help: Hold up an object: Ni cha nani? Answer with the owner first, then the possessive.
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T5_MATUMIZI_YA_ANGU_NA_.V.feedback: Mwenye kitu ni nani? Mimi: changu; yeye: chake; wao: chao. (letu)
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T5_MATUMIZI_YA_ANGU_NA_.V.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.SARUFI.T5_MATUMIZI_YA_ANGU_NA_.V.error: Puts the possessive before the noun (yangu kalamu), in English word order.
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T5_MATUMIZI_YA_ANGU_NA_.V.cause: English puts "my" before the noun; Kiswahili puts it after.
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T5_MATUMIZI_YA_ANGU_NA_.V.reveals: The question "Ni lipi sahihi?" with "yangu kalamu" among the options.
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T5_MATUMIZI_YA_ANGU_NA_.V.help: Build the phrase with cards: the noun first, then the possessive.
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T5_MATUMIZI_YA_ANGU_NA_.V.feedback: Nomino kwanza, kimilikishi baadaye: kalamu yangu. (kalamu yangu)
KISW.G1.SARUFI.T5_MATUMIZI_YA_ANGU_NA_.V.source: English or mother-tongue interference on Kiswahili; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

example.question: Mwalimu anasema "damu". Neno lipi limetamkwa vizuri?

KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T6_MATAMSHI_BORA.MATAMSHI.cause: Many Kenyan first languages have no /d/, or do not separate it from /t/; the child puts in the home sound.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T6_MATAMSHI_BORA.MATAMSHI.reveals: The question "Mwalimu anasema "damu". Neno lipi limetamkwa vizuri?" with "tamu" among the options.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T6_MATAMSHI_BORA.MATAMSHI.help: Say the two side by side, slowly, watching the mouth; the child holds up a card for the sound he hears.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T6_MATAMSHI_BORA.MATAMSHI.source: mother-tongue sound interference common in Kenyan classrooms; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T6_MATAMSHI_BORA.MATAMSHI.cause: /z/ and /s/ are close; a first language with only one of them puts that one in both places.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T6_MATAMSHI_BORA.MATAMSHI.reveals: The question "Neno lipi limetamkwa vizuri?" with "siwa" among the options.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T6_MATAMSHI_BORA.MATAMSHI.help: Contrast the two with a mirror and a hand before the mouth; the child says which he hears.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T6_MATAMSHI_BORA.MATAMSHI.source: mother-tongue sound interference common in Kenyan classrooms; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T6_MATAMSHI_BORA.MATAMSHI.error: Splits "sikio" by letters rather than by syllables (each Kiswahili syllable ends in a vowel).
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T6_MATAMSHI_BORA.MATAMSHI.cause: The child has learnt letters one by one and has not been shown that a syllable is a sound that ends in a vowel.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T6_MATAMSHI_BORA.MATAMSHI.reveals: The question "Neno "sikio" lina silabi zipi?" with "s-i-k-i-o" among the options.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T6_MATAMSHI_BORA.MATAMSHI.help: Clap the word: one clap per vowel; the consonants go with the vowel after them.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T6_MATAMSHI_BORA.MATAMSHI.feedback: Kila silabi ya Kiswahili huishia kwa irabu: si-ki-o.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T6_MATAMSHI_BORA.MATAMSHI.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T6_MATAMSHI_BORA.MATAMSHI.error: Says the English letter name instead of the Kiswahili sound (/g/ as "ji"), so the syllable cannot be built.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T6_MATAMSHI_BORA.MATAMSHI.cause: English letter names are taught alongside and the child brings them to Kiswahili; a syllable is built from sounds, not names.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T6_MATAMSHI_BORA.MATAMSHI.reveals: The question "Sauti ya herufi "g" ni ipi?" with "ji" among the options.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T6_MATAMSHI_BORA.MATAMSHI.help: Say the sound alone, short (/g/), then join it to a vowel: ga, ge, gi.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T6_MATAMSHI_BORA.MATAMSHI.source: English or mother-tongue interference on Kiswahili; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T6_MATAMSHI_BORA.MATAMSHI.error: Picks a word with no target sound when asked for one that has it.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T6_MATAMSHI_BORA.MATAMSHI.cause: The child looks at the first letter or the picture, not at the sound.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T6_MATAMSHI_BORA.MATAMSHI.reveals: The question "Ni neno lipi lina sauti /s/, /b/, /y/, /z/, /g/, /d/?" with "mkono" among the options.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T6_MATAMSHI_BORA.MATAMSHI.help: Underline the target sound in each word on the card before choosing.
KISW.G1.KUSIKI.T6_MATAMSHI_BORA.MATAMSHI.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T6_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA_S.K.error: Reads the target word wrongly: "damu" as "tamu".
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T6_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA_S.K.cause: The child reads the letters with the sounds of his first language, or adds a vowel to break the cluster.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T6_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA_S.K.reveals: The question "Neno "damu" linasomwa vipi?" with "tamu" among the options.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T6_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA_S.K.help: Pick out the target words before reading; practise them on cards, then read the passage.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T6_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA_S.K.source: mother-tongue sound interference common in Kenyan classrooms; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T6_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA_S.K.error: Reads word by word or syllable by syllable, so the sentence has no meaning when heard.

example.question: Ni usomaji upi ni wa ufasaha: "Baba ana sikio na bega."?

KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T6_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA_S.K.cause: The child is still decoding each word; he has not yet read a group of words as one piece.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T6_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA_S.K.reveals: The question "Ni usomaji upi ni wa ufasaha: "Baba ana sikio na bega."?" with "Baba ... ana ... sikio ... na ... bega." among the options.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T6_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA_S.K.help: Echo reading: the teacher reads a phrase, the child repeats it in one breath.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T6_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA_S.K.feedback: Soma maneno kwa pamoja kama unavyozungumza.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T6_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA_S.K.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T6_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA_S.K.error: Reads so softly (or so loudly, shouting) that the class cannot follow.

example.question: Unaposoma mbele ya darasa, sauti yako inafaa kuwa vipi?
example.wrong_answer: ya chini ili nisikosee mbele ya wenzangu
example.correct_answer: ya kusikika na wote darasani, bila kupiga kelele

KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T6_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA_S.K.cause: Shyness, or the belief that reading well means reading loud.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T6_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA_S.K.reveals: The question "Unaposoma mbele ya darasa, sauti yako inafaa kuwa vipi?" with "ya chini ili nisikosee mbele ya wenzangu" among the options.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T6_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA_S.K.help: Stand the reader at the front and a listener at the back: the listener raises a hand when he hears every word.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T6_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA_S.K.feedback: Soma kwa sauti inayosikika na wote, bila kupiga kelele.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T6_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA_S.K.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T6_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA_S.K.error: Reads as fast as possible and thinks the fastest reader is the best.

example.question: Kasi ifaayo ya kusoma kifungu ni ipi?
example.correct_answer: kasi ya kuzungumza, karibu maneno 20 kwa dakika

KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T6_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA_S.K.cause: Reading races in class reward speed; nobody asked whether the listeners understood.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T6_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA_S.K.reveals: The question "Kasi ifaayo ya kusoma kifungu ni ipi?" with "haraka iwezekanavyo" among the options.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T6_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA_S.K.help: Time two readings, one very fast and one at speaking pace; the listeners answer one question after each.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T6_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA_S.K.feedback: Kasi ifaayo ni ya kuzungumza: si haraka mno, si polepole mno.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T6_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA_S.K.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T6_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA_S.K.error: Reads a question in the flat voice of a statement and runs on through the koma and kikomo.

example.question: Sentensi "Je, goti lako linauma?" inasomwa vipi?
example.wrong_answer: kwa sauti ileile ya sentensi ya kawaida
example.correct_answer: sauti hupanda mwishoni kwa sababu ni swali

KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T6_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA_S.K.cause: The child looks at the words and not at the marks.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T6_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA_S.K.reveals: The question "Sentensi "Je, goti lako linauma?" inasomwa vipi?" with "kwa sauti ileile ya sentensi ya kawaida" among the options.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T6_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA_S.K.help: Read the same words three ways (. ? !); the child points at the mark that fits each reading; clap at each kikomo.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T6_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA_S.K.feedback: Kiulizi (?) hupandisha sauti mwishoni; simama kidogo kwenye koma na kikomo.
KISW.G1.KUSOMA.T6_KUSOMA_KWA_UFASAHA_S.K.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUANDI.T6_TAHAJIA_IMLA.IMLA.M1_T.error: Spells the word with the sound of his first language: "damu" written "tamu".
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T6_TAHAJIA_IMLA.IMLA.M1_T.cause: The child writes as he says the word; if his first language merges the two sounds, the letter is a guess.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T6_TAHAJIA_IMLA.IMLA.M1_T.reveals: The question "Ni tahajia ipi sahihi?" with "tamu" among the options.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T6_TAHAJIA_IMLA.IMLA.M1_T.help: Keep a list of the class's hard pairs (l/r, s/sh, z/dh, s/th); say each word slowly before writing.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T6_TAHAJIA_IMLA.IMLA.M1_T.feedback: Andika "damu" kama linavyotamkwa kwa Kiswahili sanifu.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T6_TAHAJIA_IMLA.IMLA.M1_T.source: mother-tongue sound interference common in Kenyan classrooms; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUANDI.T6_TAHAJIA_IMLA.IMLA.M1_T.cause: The n or m before a consonant is soft and quick; the child does not hear it.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T6_TAHAJIA_IMLA.IMLA.M1_T.reveals: The question "Ni tahajia ipi sahihi?" with "devu" among the options.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T6_TAHAJIA_IMLA.IMLA.M1_T.help: Hum the nasal before the word (mmm-bwa, nnn-dege).
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T6_TAHAJIA_IMLA.IMLA.M1_T.source: mother-tongue sound interference common in Kenyan classrooms; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUANDI.T6_TAHAJIA_IMLA.IMLA.M1_T.error: Writes a long vowel short, so the word changes: "kaa" written "ka".
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T6_TAHAJIA_IMLA.IMLA.M1_T.cause: The child hears the length but does not know it is shown by two letters.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T6_TAHAJIA_IMLA.IMLA.M1_T.reveals: The question "Andika neno lenye maana ya "kuketi"." with "ka" among the options.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T6_TAHAJIA_IMLA.IMLA.M1_T.help: Clap the two vowels as two beats; compare a word with one and two vowels.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T6_TAHAJIA_IMLA.IMLA.M1_T.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUANDI.T6_TAHAJIA_IMLA.IMLA.M1_T.error: Writes ng' without the apostrophe (ngombe for ng'ombe), or puts it where it does not belong (ng'oma for ngoma).

example.question: Ni tahajia ipi sahihi ya mnyama anayetupa maziwa?

KISW.G1.KUANDI.T6_TAHAJIA_IMLA.IMLA.M1_T.cause: Ng' and ng are two sounds; the apostrophe looks like dirt on the page to the child.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T6_TAHAJIA_IMLA.IMLA.M1_T.reveals: The question "Ni tahajia ipi sahihi ya mnyama anayetupa maziwa?" with "ngombe" among the options.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T6_TAHAJIA_IMLA.IMLA.M1_T.help: Say ng'ombe and ngoma: the first has no g sound; mark it with the apostrophe.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T6_TAHAJIA_IMLA.IMLA.M1_T.source: common learner error; to confirm by a native Kiswahili teacher

KISW.G1.KUANDI.T6_TAHAJIA_IMLA.IMLA.M1_T.error: Joins two words into one, or splits one word into two (kwasababu; mwana funzi).
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T6_TAHAJIA_IMLA.IMLA.M1_T.cause: In speech the words run together; the child has not seen each written apart.
KISW.G1.KUANDI.T6_TAHAJIA_IMLA.IMLA.M1_T.reveals: The question "Ni lipi sahihi?" with "Nilichelewa kwasababu ya mvua." among the options.
